newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics down despite good US indicator.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics down despite good US indicator.

text.p: Taiwan's electronic shares rose slightly at Wednesday's open on news that the U.S. semiconductor industry's book-to-bill ratio rose to 0.90 in August from a revised July ratio of 0.86, but then fell at mid-morning in a market-wide consolidation, brokers said.
With 75 minutes left, electronics had fallen 0.50 percent while the overall index was up 0.74 percent.
Taiwan Semiconductor fell T$1 or 1.83 percent to T$53.5 and United Microelectronics edged down 10 cents or 0.27 percent to T$36. The two are Taiwan's top chip makers.

"The good news only helped reduce profit-taking pressure on electronics, and it seems electronics may need more time to consolidate before significantly rising again," said Albert Lin of Golden Securities.
Brokers said the August ratio, while improved, was below expectations.
"August and September should be a hot-sale season for the semiconductor industry, so the August ratio, though improved, was poorer than expected," said Ben Lee of Nomura Securities.
"I would say Taiwan's semiconductor industry has not fully bottomed out," Lee said. "But a gradual recovery is expected."
